ut_spring_creek.blurb: A small sandstone crag south of Cedar City, on the outskirts of Zion's Kolob side, with ten routes that lean heavily toward trad and include a couple of bolted lines. Grades run from 5.8 up to the low 5.11s, with the bulk of them around 5.10. It is a walk of a mile and a half uphill into a narrow section, where the first climbs show up on your left. The area is newly developed and climbers rarely turn up, so expect the canyon largely to yourself.

ut_training_camp.blurb: A cluster of buttresses above Provo, at Rock Canyon's mouth on the north side. Ten routes, nearly all sport with a single trad line, mostly from 5.6 to 5.10 with one easy outlier. The rock is quartzite, and the page warns that a crumbly pale layer at the bottom has to be scrambled through before the sturdier reddish and yellowish stone above. The buttresses sit over a steep grassy slope that drops to the creek bed, and you reach them by traversing along the base on sheep trails rather than cutting straight up.

ut_wild_the.blurb: A compact crag in Rock Canyon near Provo, first on the left a short way up the gully. The ten routes are short but well regarded, mostly sport with three trad lines, running from 5.5 into the 5.10 range with most in the 5.7 bracket. Several are pocketed slabs, and a few cracks take gear. Trees give plenty of shade, and the wall stays shaded until about 1:30 in the afternoon. That, and the mellow grades, makes it a natural pick for groups, classes and anyone building skills. Watch for rattlesnakes at the base.

ut_dark_star_gully.blurb: A steep little gully in Big Cottonwood Canyon with ten routes split evenly between sport and trad. It is a harder-leaning venue: grades start at 5.8 but most of the climbing falls between 5.10 and 5.11, with one route in the 5.12 range. The wall faces mostly west with a hint of south, so it runs warm. Poison ivy or oak grows in the upper reaches, and a few lines sit right beside the stream and can be wet in spring. Most climbs have good anchors, so getting down is straightforward.

vt_lower_ragnarock.blurb: A sport-leaning crag in Smugglers' Notch, in the rock bands right of Elephant's Head Buttress and beside the Ragnarock ice route. Ten routes, seven of them bolted and three trad, with grades from 5.9 to 5.13 and the centre of gravity around 5.10 to 5.11. Part of the climbing is on a small buttress left of the ice flow, and part on a lower wall roughly 200 feet to its right. The cliffs lie south of Elephant's Head and catch warm afternoon sun. Development here is recent.

vt_outhouse_boulder.blurb: A boulder in Smugglers' Notch tucked behind the main parking lot and visitor center. Its main block leans against a neighbour to make a tunnel-like space, and a small stream usually runs through it. Ten problems cover a wide range, from around V2 up to V12, with a handful of easy-to-moderate lines, one around V6 and a hard cluster from V10 to V12. It is a short walk up the stream from the outhouses, or downhill from the Nemesis boulder.

vt_carcass_crag.blurb: A small cliff in the Bolton area of northern Vermont, noted for good-quality stone. Ten routes, around seven bolted and three trad, from 5.9 up to 5.12, with most sitting in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits climbers who already lead hard. Expect it to be fairly shady, and it can stay damp with some seepage. The hike from the trail is shorter than the one to neighbouring 82 Crag, and in early spring or late fall the cliff shows through the trees before the final bend.
